slot.brief: Two cells of different emfs and internal resistances in parallel across a resistor; find equivalent emf of the combination and current through the external resistor.

stem: Two cells of emf $2$ V and $6$ V, with internal resistances $2\ \text{Ω}$ and $6\ \text{Ω}$ respectively, are connected in parallel with like terminals joined across a $1.5\ \text{Ω}$ resistor. Find the equivalent emf and the current through the resistor.

verdicts.working: For like terminals joined, the equivalent emf is (2/2 + 6/6)/(1/2 + 1/6) = 3 V. The equivalent internal resistance is 2 parallel 6 = 1.5 ohm, so the resistor current is 3/(1.5 + 1.5) = 1 A.

working:
$\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{2/2+6/6}{1/2+1/6}=3\ \text{V}$
$r_{\text{eq}}=2\parallel6=1.5\ \text{Ω}$
$I=\dfrac{3}{1.5+1.5}=1\ \text{A}$

Independent check: For like terminals joined, the equivalent emf is (2/2 + 6/6)/(1/2 + 1/6) = 3 V. The equivalent internal resistance is 2 parallel 6 = 1.5 ohm, so the resistor current is 3/(1.5 + 1.5) = 1 A.
solution:
For cells in parallel with like terminals, $\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{E_1/r_1+E_2/r_2}{1/r_1+1/r_2}=\dfrac{2/2+6/6}{1/2+1/6}=3\,\text{V}$.  
The equivalent internal resistance is $r_{\text{eq}}=2\parallel6=1.5\,\Omega$.  
$$I=\frac{\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}}{r_{\text{eq}}+R}=\frac{3}{1.5+1.5}=1\,\text{A}$$
